alignments.note: Finite verb with its English subject pronoun; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
3fp suffix rendered by the object pronoun them (rule 18).
Prohibitive אַל rendered by not, discontinuous from the verb it negates under rule 25.
Jussive verb of calling rendered Call.
Dative לְ recast as a bare English indirect object, leaving the preposition no word of its own (rule 40).
1cs suffix rendered by the object pronoun me (rules 18, 40).
Proper name Naomi; the marginal gloss That is, Pleasant is read and set aside under rule 38.
Second dative לְ likewise left with no English word by the bare indirect object (rule 40).
Proper name Mara; the marginal gloss That is, Bitter is read and set aside under rule 38.
כִּי rendered by the causal for.

Hiphil of מָרַר rendered by the light verb phrase hath dealt ... bitterly; the head is the complement carrying the lexeme, since dealt alone deals anything (rule 44). The unit is discontinuous around very under rule 25.
Divine title שַׁדַּי with the supplied the, which determines the nominal expression and is not added (rule 15); head on the word carrying the lexeme.
לְ rendered by the written with; the ASV spends a word on this preposition's own relation, so rule 40 does not reach it.
Adverb מְאֹד rendered very, standing inside the verb phrase and so splitting that unit under rule 25.

review_notes: Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once; the two datives of לִי are unrepresented under rule 40 while their suffixes take the written me.
hath dealt ... bitterly heads on bitterly under rule 44's light-verb clause; the competing head would be dealt, which is the English light verb and writes nothing of מרר.
The third לְ is aligned rather than unrepresented because the ASV writes with for its own relation.
Both ASV marginal notes were read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text governs.
